card.title: Senior Manager, Engineering Continuous Improvement
card.description:
**Logistics at full potential.**

At GXO, we’re constantly looking for talented individuals at all levels who can deliver the caliber of service our company requires. You know that a positive work environment creates happy employees, which boosts productivity and dedication. On our team, you’ll have the support to excel at work and the resources to build a career you can be proud of.

 

As the **Senior Manager, Solutions Engineering**, you will lead a team that connects Solution Design, Implementation, and Operations across GXO's OmniChannel Retail and Ecommerce divisions. You will provide operational expertise throughout the customer lifecycle, from early-stage RFPs and solution assessments through implementation, site launch, go-live, and operational stabilization. You will lead teams in evaluating facility designs, process flows, staffing requirements, automation strategies, and operational risks while driving continuous improvement, cost savings, and productivity initiatives across the network.

**Pay, benefits and more.** 
We are eager to attract the best, so we offer competitive compensation and a generous benefits package, including full health insurance (medical, dental and vision), 401(k), life insurance, disability and more.

**What you'll do on a typical day:**

* Lead Solutions Engineering activities throughout the RFP, implementation, and operational lifecycle, providing Operations input on facility design, productivity rates, automation strategies, staffing requirements, and other key solution elements
* Provide subject-matter expertise on warehouse operations, labor requirements, WMS, automation capabilities, and operational constraints to ensure solutions are practical and executable
* Review proposed KPIs, SLAs, contractual requirements, solution assumptions, and cost models while identifying and escalating risks that could impact operational performance
* Partner with Implementations, Operations, HR, Analytics, and customers during joint planning and implementation to validate assumptions, develop volume and headcount ramp plans, and ensure the solution delivered matches the solution designed
* Lead Production Readiness Testing, develop solution-specific test cases, support User Acceptance Testing, and ensure KPI reporting is established prior to go-live
* Provide on-site support through site launch, go-live, and hypercare, helping Operations teams stabilize performance and transition to full operational ownership
* Identify and lead Continuous Improvement initiatives that deliver cost savings, productivity improvements, process optimization, and other business improvements across the network
* Develop business cases, conduct root-cause analysis, time studies, simulations, pilots, and process improvement activities, and present recommendations and validated results to leadership and Finance
* Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team while establishing clear expectations, accountability, performance goals, and career development opportunities

**What you need to succeed at GXO:**

**At a minimum, you'll need:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or equivalent related work or military experience
* 8+ years of related work experience
* Strong knowledge and experience in Lean Manufacturing and/or Continuous Improvement
* Advanced analytical skills with the ability to analyze complex data, processes, systems, and procedures
* Extensive knowledge of warehouse operations, supply chain management, and warehouse production environments
* Expertise in Warehouse Management Systems (WMS), supply chain automation, warehousing solutions, and production planning methodologies
* Strong knowledge of Lean Warehousing and warehouse/supply chain processes
* Experience using analytical and process improvement tools, including flow charts, Pareto charts, cause-and-effect diagrams, and run charts
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to present complex information clearly to various audiences
* Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite

**It'd be great if you also have:**

* Master's degree in Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field
* 2+ years of leadership experience
* Experience owning the development, enhancement, and maintenance of end-to-end solutions and deliverables
* Experience using AutoCAD to develop facility layouts and detailed work areas
* Lean or Six Sigma Black Belt certification
* Expert data management and SQL skills

**We engineer faster, smarter, leaner supply chains.**

GXO is a leading provider of cutting-edge supply chain solutions to the most successful companies in the world. We help our customers manage their goods most efficiently using our technology and services. Our greatest strength is our global team – energetic, innovative people of all experience levels and talents who make GXO a great place to work.

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer including Disabled/Veterans.

GXO adheres to CDC, OSHA and state and local requirements regarding COVID safety. All employees and visitors are expected to comply with GXO policies which are in place to safeguard our employees and customers.

All applicants who receive a conditional offer of employment may be required to take and pass a pre-employment drug test.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required of personnel so classified. All employees may be required to perform duties outside of their normal responsibilities from time to time, as needed. Review GXO's candidate privacy statement here.

card.title: Plant Manager
card.description:
**Plant Manager.**

**Wichita, Kansas.**

**Full-time.**

**PSC INDUSTRIES.**

**Job Summary:** 
The Plant Manager will be working for a Progressive and Growing Manufacturing Organization. The Plant Manager is responsible for general supervision of all phases of plant operations including production, materials, quality control, maintenance, receiving & shipping, daily P&L, R&D, purchasing/procurement, finance/accounting, and customer-related sales along with business development. 
 
**Main Duties & Responsibilities:** 
**Production:**

* Tracking operating efficiencies.
* Managing labor expenditures.
* Reducing scrap.
* Continuously improving production thru Kaizen events, Kanban systems, SMED workshops.
* Strong adherence to 5-S principles.
* Define, research and specify any new equipment needs.
* Specify layouts for all new tooling requirements with a focus on material utilization and profitability.

**Quality/Service:**

* Instill a facility-wide commitment to 100% on-time delivery of all products.
* Implement, follow and continuously improve corporate and facility QMS.
* Consistently reduce annual PPM rate.

**Sales:**

* Identifying new business, both organically and through new contacts.
* Visit existing customers on a regular basis to maintain positive communication with OEM buyers, production leaders, design engineers and quality engineers.
* Provide return of all requested quotes in less than 24 hours of receipt.

**Finance:**

* Create cost and payback analysis for new capital asset requests.
* Maintain facility asset list.

**Safety:**

* Demonstrate the leadership required to maintain an accident-free facility.
* Facilitate monthly safety training for all employees per corporate and OSHA requirements.

**Materials/Inventory:**

* Ensure inventory is maintained with a focus on 8 turns annually.
* Ensure all BOM are up to date and accurate per the costing process.
* Specifying new material requirements.
* Negotiating with raw material suppliers to maintain a positive costing position.

**Required Qualification & Experience:**

* Bachelor’s degree preferred.
* 5+ years’ management experience in a manufacturing environment.
* Experience and/or understanding of the Aerospace supply industry preferred.
* Experience working within a documented quality system.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office, especially Excel.
* Experience with Lean Application Methodologies.
* CAD experience preferred.
* Understanding of the OEM market drivers and pressures preferred.
* Knowledge of converting processes and techniques preferred.
* Operational understanding of ISO/AS9100.
* Travel up to 25%.

**Supervisory Responsibilities:**

* Directly supervises all department heads in the facility**.** Responsibilities include **i**nterviewing, hiring, training, planning, directing work, appraising performance, addressing complaints and resolving problems.

**Physical Demands:**

* While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel objects, tools, or controls and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, sit, reach with hands and arms, and climb or balance.

card.title: Industrial Gases Plant Manager
card.description:
**Position Summary**

The Industrial Gases Plant Manager is responsible for the safe, reliable, and cost-effective operation of an industrial gases production facility, ensuring uninterrupted production and supply of products such as oxygen, nitrogen, argon, hydrogen, and CO₂. The role provides leadership for operations, maintenance, safety, quality, and continuous improvement while meeting business, customer, and regulatory requirements.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead all plant operations to achieve safety, production, quality, and reliability targets.
* Ensure compliance with environmental, health, safety, and process safety management (PSM) standards.
* Drive operational excellence through continuous improvement, productivity, and energy-efficiency initiatives.
* Oversee maintenance and reliability programs to maximize plant uptime and asset performance.
* Manage plant budgets, operating costs, and capital improvement projects.
* Lead, coach, and develop plant personnel, fostering a culture of accountability and high performance.
* Ensure compliance with quality systems, customer specifications, and regulatory requirements.
* Coordinate with supply chain, logistics, engineering, and commercial teams to ensure uninterrupted product supply.
* Lead root cause investigations and implement corrective and preventive actions.
* Support plant expansions, upgrades, and commissioning activities.

**Management Responsibilities**

Directly manages plant leadership and operational personnel, including maintenance, operations, and technical staff. Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, training, coaching, performance management, disciplinary action, succession planning, and employee development.

**Other Duties**

This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications associated with the position. Duties and responsibilities may be modified at any time to meet the business needs of the organization.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
* 8+ years of experience in industrial gases, chemicals, petrochemicals, refining, or other continuous process industries.
* 5+ years of leadership experience managing industrial gases plant operations.
* Strong knowledge of cryogenic processes, compressors, rotating equipment, utilities, and process control systems.
* Experience with DCS/PLC systems, reliability practices, and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.

**Key Competencies**

* Safety Leadership
* Operational Excellence
* Team Development
* Financial & Business Acumen
* Reliability & Asset Management
* Strategic Thinking
* Communication & Stakeholder Management

**Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)**

* Safety performance and regulatory compliance
* Plant availability and reliability
* Production efficiency and energy consumption
* Product quality performance
* Budget and cost management
* Employee engagement and development
* Customer supply reliability

**Reports To**: President Plants and Operation Department

**Direct Reports**: Maintenance Manager and Plant Operations Team.

**Work Environment**

This position operates primarily within an industrial manufacturing environment and office setting. The Plant Manager regularly works in and around production equipment, compressors, cryogenic systems, utilities, and other industrial process operations. The role routinely uses standard office equipment, including computers, phones, scanners, and related technology. Frequent interaction with plant employees, contractors, customers, regulatory agencies, and corporate leadership is required. Occasional travel to company facilities, customer sites, industry meetings, and training programs may be required.

**Physical Demands**

This role requires a combination of office-based and plant-floor activities. The employee is frequently required to sit, stand, walk, climb stairs and ladders, communicate effectively, and use a computer for extended periods. The position may require working in varying environmental conditions, including exposure to industrial noise, temperature fluctuations, and process equipment. The ability to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety glasses, hard hats, hearing protection, steel-toed footwear, and other safety equipment as required, is essential. The employee may occasionally be required to lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.

**Position Type and Expected Hours of Work**

This is a full-time exempt position. The Plant Manager is expected to maintain a schedule sufficient to meet business and operational needs. Due to the nature of continuous industrial operations, the position may require availability outside normal business hours, including evenings, weekends, holidays, emergency response situations, planned maintenance outages, and on-call responsibilities as needed.

**Work Authorization**

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States and must maintain eligibility to work in the U.S. throughout their employment. Appropriate documentation authorizing employment in the United States is required upon hire.

**Equal Employment Opportunity Statement**

Air Water America is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to attracting, developing, and retaining a diverse workforce and fostering an inclusive work environment where all employees are treated with dignity and respect. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, protected veteran status, military status, or any other status protected under applicable federal, state, or local laws. Air Water America complies with all applicable equal employment opportunity laws and regulations and provides reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and religious observances as required by law.

card.title: Plant Manager (Yokosuka, Japan)
card.description:
**NORESCO, an OPTERRA Company**, helps customers modernize aging building systems and upgrade energy and water infrastructure to meet evolving demands. We implement innovative energy efficiency, distributed generation, energy storage, and renewable energy solutions that optimize the operational efficiency and improve resilience of buildings, campuses, military installations, and communities.

We are seeking an on-site Project Manager to oversee all preventive, corrective, and major maintenance activities (including repair and replacement work) at NORESCO’s 40 MW electric and thermal production facility at Yokosuka Naval Base, Japan. The cogeneration plant (CGS) is a critical asset for the base and daily operations are conducted by Navy personnel in partnership with NORESCO and our subcontractors.

NORESCO constructed the plant, which generates 50Hz and 60Hz power as well as a combination of Soft and Pure Steam, in 2008 under a Federal Energy Savings Performance Contract (ESPC). The plant pays for itself out of energy savings which NORESCO has guaranteed for the past 18 years. In order to meet our savings and availability guarantees, we employ a robust preventive maintenance program which relies heavily on Long Term Service Agreements (LTSAs) for all major pieces of equipment.

This is a Senior level position reporting to NORESCO’s Operations Manager and is administered through a 3 to 5 year International Assignment Agreement (IAA). This agreement is negotiated with each of our employees working Outside of the Continental Unites States (OCONUS). The agreement includes consideration for overseas pay, benefits, healthcare, housing, food, travel, vacation, stateside visits, relocation, etc., and is customized to the unique requirements of each new hire.

You will be the primary liaison between our NAVY customers, Japanese operators and subcontractors, as well as NORESCO team to ensure contractual obligations are met. While many of the team members in Japan speak English or are Bi-Lingual, some are not. Translators are available to facilitate conversations or process written correspondence as necessary. Japan is an amazing culture with many unique customs and protocols, a willingness to learn and adapt to their approach is an important part of your success.

It is of utmost importance for you to possess good listening, communication, and computer skills in addition to being proactive, organized, and having a bias for action. The Yokosuka Project Manager is supported by (and in-turn supports) many other NORESCO departments; Development, Engineering, Commissioning, O&M, M&V, Accounting, Legal, etc. Cross-functional technical skills, adaptability, versatility, and a quest for continuous learning and integration of advances are key in this position.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Overall contractual responsibility for plant maintenance and repair activities through careful management of Long-Term Service Agreements (LTSAs) and work orders.
* Ensuring subcontractor work is performed in a safe and professional manner with materials that meet or exceed applicable Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and Regulatory standards.
* Participate in scheduled operations meetings and coordinate upcoming maintenance activities within the defined expectations and constraints of the customer and subcontractor availability.
* Prepare and distribute standard monthly reports (that summarize operations, maintenance, and repair activities) to NORESCO management, key customer contacts, and other stakeholders.
* Review plant operations logs, alarms, and performance data on a regular basis to evaluate equipment condition, collaborate with NORESCO team to identify potential issues.
* Perform plant inspections and safety walkthroughs during regular operations, confirm changes in equipment line-up, and subcontractor compliance with typical maintenance activities.
* Support Profit and Loss (P&L) management; assist with generating and maintaining the annual budget; capital expenditure planning; monthly forecasts, accruals, and variance analysis with development of recovery plans as needed to deliver the target revenue and profit.
* Review service agreements/proposals with manager; generate purchase orders as required; provide initial review and approval of invoices for materials and services.
* Collaborate with LTSA contractors to plan work and identify resources required for shutdown tasks such as parts, tooling, equipment, materials, and work procedures. Review and confirm subcontractors’ detailed work plans meet the customer and project needs.
* Maintain NORESCO’s Computer Maintenance Management System (CMMS) to generate reports for maintenance schedules, completion status reports, equipment histories, and forecasts.
* Coordinate with subcontractors, visitors and customers to ensure protocols are followed on matters related to site access, security clearance, safety measures, and work permits.
* Monitor warranty programs to ensure the planned and required coverage is maintained by complying with all warranty requirements. Ensure warranty work is claimed in a timely manner, and all warranty issues are resolved to minimize out of pocket expenses.
* Monitor and analyze facility performance and host data for equipment and systems condition assessments. Review finings with Operations Manger and adjust maintenance plans accordingly.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelors degree, Associates degree, or equivalent Technical Training (ex; Navy Nuclear)
* 5+ years of experience in one of the following fields; electric power generation, cogeneration, industrial utility, or district energy industry with strong working knowledge of equipment
* Ability to obtain a Federal Security Clearance for work at Government facilities.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**:

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, project management discipline or equivalent experience
* High level communication, leadership, technical, and project management skills.
* Strong sense of ownership and focus on maintaining; a Safe work environment, Uninterrupted Plant operations, Quality control, Project schedule, Resolving issues in a timely manner, and consistently meeting deadlines and commitments.
* Graduate degree in engineering or business administration
* Strong interest in engaging operators, customers, and partners to grow relationships.
* Advanced knowledge of one or more facets of Engineering or Central Plants operations; design principles, technologies, equipment maintenance and troubleshooting.
* Energy optimization, utility rates, energy costs, applicable codes, design guides, and standards.
* Robust combination of business acumen, risk management, and strategic thinking skills.
* US military or DOD project management experience, Japanese language skills, and international work experience are a plus.

**Physical requirements include:**

* Ability to climb stairs and fixed ladders.
* Ability to access rooftops and elevated work areas while following safety protocols.
* Ability to work at heights and in confined or industrial environments as required.
* Ability to maintain balance and mobility while navigating mechanical, utility, and production areas.

**Compensation:**

* $130,000 – $150,000 per year, depending on experience + bonuses

**Benefits:**

* HSA Medical insurance, with a choice of 2 buy-up options
* Dental insurance
* Vision insurance
* 100% Safe Harbor 401(k) match
* 100% company paid Life insurance
* 100% company paid Long-term Disability insurance
* Short-term Disability insurance
* Flexible Spending Account
* Commuter Benefits
* Legal and Identity Protection
* Pet Insurance Coverage
* Fertility and Reproductive Health
* Generous Paid Time Off, including Holiday, Vacation, and Sick Pay

card.title: Production Strategy & Operations Director
card.description:
**Position Overview**

JHB Group, Inc. is seeking a highly organized, detail-oriented, and forward-thinking Production Strategy & Operations Director to lead production planning, operational coordination, process development, and efficiency improvements within our specialty vehicle and trailer manufacturing facility.

**Successful production starts before the work begins—with planning, preparation, organization, and communication.** This leadership role focuses on creating the systems, schedules, workflows, and accountability that help teams execute complex custom manufacturing projects consistently and efficiently. Manufacturing experience is a strong advantage, but exceptional organizational and operational leadership skills are the priority.

**Key Responsibilities**

Strategic Production Planning & Scheduling

* Develop and maintain master production schedules across multiple custom projects.

* Translate project requirements and delivery commitments into actionable daily, weekly, and long-term plans.

* Coordinate labor, materials, equipment, and other resources to support production priorities.

* Anticipate scheduling conflicts, capacity limitations, and bottlenecks before they affect deadlines.

* Monitor milestones and adjust plans proactively as project requirements change.

**Operational Organization & Preparation**

* Ensure drawings, work instructions, tools, equipment, and materials are ready before work begins.

* Coordinate with purchasing, inventory, engineering, and production to confirm project readiness.

* Create clear systems for tracking tasks, outstanding issues, and production status.

* Improve material staging, work-area organization, and shop readiness.

* Reduce downtime caused by missing parts, unclear instructions, and inadequate preparation.

**Process Development & Continuous Improvement**

* Evaluate workflows and implement practical improvements to productivity and consistency.

* Develop, document, implement, and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs).

* Establish repeatable processes and performance-tracking systems across departments.

* Identify root causes of recurring delays, rework, and wasted labor; implement lasting solutions.

* Promote continuous improvement, operational discipline, and accountability.

**Production Execution & Coordination**

* Coordinate fabrication, welding, electrical, carpentry, cabinetry, assembly, and finishing activities.

* Align work assignments with production schedules and available resources.

* Facilitate timely communication and handoffs between departments.• Identify and resolve production constraints through planning and cross-functional coordination.

* Maintain accurate visibility into progress, priorities, and upcoming requirements.

Leadership, Communication & Accountability

* Set clear expectations and priorities for production personnel and department leaders.

* Lead concise daily production meetings and weekly planning reviews.

* Hold teams accountable for schedules, productivity, quality, safety, and procedures.

* Support training, staffing coordination, and constructive performance feedback.

* Model professionalism, organization, ownership, and follow-through.

Quality & Operational Performance

* Coordinate quality checkpoints and confirm work aligns with drawings and project specifications.

* Identify recurring workmanship issues and establish corrective processes.

* Track schedule adherence, labor utilization, milestones, and production performance.

* Provide management with accurate reporting on progress, risks, and resource needs.

* Establish measurable operational goals and evaluate results.

**Required Skills & Attributes**

* Exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail.

* Strong strategic planning, scheduling, prioritization, and project coordination abilities.

* Ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities in a changing environment.

* Proactive approach to anticipating needs and preventing problems.

* Demonstrated ability to implement processes, communicate expectations, and drive follow-through.

* Strong analytical, problem-solving, leadership, and interpersonal skills.

* Proficiency with spreadsheets, scheduling tools, and operational tracking systems.

* Ability to work independently and make sound operational decisions.

Preferred Experience

* Five or more years in operations management, production planning, project management, manufacturing, or a related

field.

* Experience coordinating teams and departments, developing SOPs, or improving workflows.

* Background in manufacturing, fabrication, automotive, specialty vehicles, or custom assembly.

* Familiarity with bills of materials, inventory, resource planning, and production drawings.

* Experience with Lean Manufacturing, 5S, or other continuous improvement practices.

Manufacturing experience is preferred, not required. Candidates from operations, logistics, or project planning

backgrounds with outstanding organizational and leadership capabilities are encouraged to apply.

**What Success Looks Like**

* Realistic schedules, clear project milestones, and well-defined responsibilities.

* People, parts, drawings, tools, and instructions ready before each production phase begins.• Fewer avoidable delays, bottlenecks, rework cycles, and interruptions.

* Documented processes that are consistently followed and improved.

* Clear cross-department communication and accurate management visibility.

* A more predictable, efficient, organized, and scalable production operation.

**The Ideal Candidate**

You naturally bring structure to complex environments. You enjoy organizing people and resources, creating effective systems, and thinking several steps ahead. You take ownership, follow through, and understand that successful execution depends on having the right Plan. Parts. People. in place before work begins. You are motivated not merely to keep production moving, but to make it work better every day.

**About JHB Group**

JHB Group, Inc. designs and manufactures custom mobile solutions for public safety, emergency management, government, military, and commercial customers. Our products include mobile command centers, emergency response vehicles, specialty trailers, and training simulators. In-house capabilities span engineering, metal fabrication, welding, carpentry, cabinetry, electrical systems, networking, graphics, finishing, and final assembly.

**Why Join JHB Group?**

This role offers the opportunity to shape how a specialty manufacturing operation plans, organizes, measures, and executes its work. We seek a leader who wants to build effective systems, implement improvements, and contribute directly to long-term success.

**If you are a strategic thinker, exceptional organizer, and results-driven leader who believes planning and preparation are the foundation of successful operations, we encourage you to apply.**

Pay: $74,000.00 - $84,000.00 per year

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

card.title: Plant Manager
card.description:
**Job Description:** We are seeking a hands-on Plant Manager to lead all plant operations at Gates Washer. If you are a production manager, operations manager, or senior supervisor who understands the production and financial side of manufacturing and is ready to step up and run a plant, this is the right fit for you. This is the senior operations role at our facility, for someone who spends time on the floor, sets clear expectations, and builds a strong team. You will be responsible for quality, on-time delivery, productivity, and manufacturing costs.

**About our Company:**

**Who we are:** Gates Washer and Manufacturing Company, located right next to Chicago O’Hare and established in 1927, is a prominent name in specialty washers and light stampings. Our customers in the automotive, industrial, and aerospace sectors trust us for reliable products. With advanced automatic punch presses and our own tool room, we produce a wide range of parts from various metals and materials.

**Responsibilities:**

**Lead the Plant:** Manage all plant departments: punch presses, tool room, maintenance, tumbling, secondary operations, packaging, quality, shipping and receiving, and inventory.

**Run Daily Production:** Own the production schedule and daily priorities, balance labor and machine capacity, and keep work flowing to ship on time.

**Quality:** Serve as head of quality. Reduce scrap, rework, and customer returns, and make sure every job meets specification.

**People:** Hire, train, review, and when necessary let go of staff. Build cross-training and a bench of people for key positions.

**Cost and Budget:** Be responsible for parts of the P&L, including manufacturing expenses, labor, and productivity.

**Safety and Facility:** Own plant safety and compliance, keep equipment and the building maintained, and recommend equipment investments.

**Customers and Teamwork:** Work with sales and purchasing on quoting, material, and delivery dates, and deal directly with customers on quality and delivery issues.

**Reporting:** Report plant performance to ownership: on-time delivery, quality, productivity, and cost against budget.

**Continuous Improvement:** Write and maintain procedures, improve changeovers and uptime, and get the most out of our equipment.

**Skills and Qualifications:**

* 10 or more years in metal manufacturing, stamping, and fabrication. Machine shop or automotive supplier experience also considered.
* 5 or more years leading people, including at least 2 to 3 years managing a team of 10 or more.
* Working knowledge of tooling, dies, and tool room practices.
* Hands-on quality experience under a formal system such as ISO 9001.
* Experience managing budget or manufacturing costs.
* Experience hiring, reviewing, and managing performance.
* Comfortable with production metrics and an ERP or scheduling system.
* Stamping or punch press experience is preferred but not required.
* A degree is preferred but not required.
* Applicants must be legally eligible to work in the country.

**Compensation and Benefits:**

**Base Salary:** $125,000–$130,000 per year.

**Annual Performance Bonus: $15,000–$20,000**

.

**Long-Term Incentive Bonus:**

Share in the company's growth and success. If Gates increases in value over the next five years, you receive a share of that increase, with the potential for a six-figure payout.

Pay: $125,000.00 - $130,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Experience:

* Plant management: 3 years (Preferred)

Work Location: In person

card.title: Director of Manufacturing
card.description:
We are seeking a strategic, technical, and results-driven Director of Manufacturing to lead and optimize high-volume packaging blow molding facility. As a key member of the executive leadership team, you will bridge organizational strategy with daily shop floor execution by overseeing multi-shift operations, managing the operational budget, and driving performance across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and talent development. To succeed in this role, you will bring deep technical expertise in plastic blow molding technologies, automated downstream packaging, and strong financial acumen to achieve large-scale operational excellence.
 
 
In terms of strategic leadership and daily operations, you will execute manufacturing strategies that maximize throughput, cycle times, and capacity utilization across all production lines. You will oversee multi-shift operations to foster a culture of accountability and high performance on the plant floor while maintaining disciplined daily management routines, including production reviews, KPI tracking, and systematic escalation procedures. Additionally, you will translate forecasting and demand data into actionable manufacturing plans, master schedules, and staffing models designed to meet fast-paced consumer goods delivery timelines.
 
 
From a technical and equipment management perspective, you will optimize processing parameters across a diverse fleet of plastic blow molding machinery and drive high-speed automation projects. You will also oversee material management to maximize the efficiency of high-volume grades. Partner closely with Maintenance and Tooling teams to minimize changeover downtime, and enforce rigorous preventive maintenance programs.

card.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering Programs
card.description:
Are you interested in being part of an innovative team that supports Westinghouse's mission to provide clean energy solutions? At Westinghouse, we recognize that our employees are our most valuable asset and we seek to identify, attract and recruit the most qualified talent while recognizing and encouraging the value of diversity in the global workplace.
 
 
**About The Role**
As a Senior Manager of MFG Engineering Programs in our New Product Introduction group, you will be responsible and accountable to lead and deliver global nuclear fuel manufacturing project execution across Westinghouse Electric Corporation (WEC) fuel manufacturing facilities in the US, UK & Sweden operations. You will be deployed to guide progress and execution of multiple projects within our organization, based on the program needs. The Sr Manager owns the global manufacturing scope of new product introduction and is accountable to lead project execution to delivery in-full, without complaint products to our customers while meeting safety and financial goals. This position will guide interaction between Fuel Engineering, Nuclear Fuel Project Managers, Product Delivery & Commercial Managers, Product Management, Supply Chain, SIOP, Plant Manufacturing Managers, Global Quality, and Supplier or customer teams. It will also coordinate on project deliverables, issues, and resolution. Program budget accountability ranges from $1M - $20M.
 
 
You will report to the Director of New Product Introduction and support the role remotely with 25 - 35% travel between global manufacturing facilities.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Comprehend entire program scope, such as commercial, licensing, regulatory and initiate appropriate scope within the manufacturing program scope.
* Support project task-based schedules and track/report milestone progress against the program management plan.
* Deploy strategies for optimizing and streamlining legacy fuel manufacturing operations in partnership with manufacturing sites and functional leads.
* Analyze existing processes and identify value-added and non-value-added activities to solve design challenges.
* Manage project risks and opportunities to closure in partnership with functional leads and Program Managers. Identify issues, propose solutions and lead recovery plans to closure.
* Implement within project schedule and budget, tracking expenses and identifying cost-savings opportunities. Communicate with partners, providing updates on project milestones, risks, critical escalations and issues.
* Present strategic project reports, status updates, and performance metrics to senior leadership and important partners.
* Identify areas of improvement or gaps in current processes and develop strategies to promote efficiency and productivity in new product and process introduction.
* Perform as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) to support project teams in new product and process development such as APQP and PPAP industry standards.
* Compare actual performance against planned performance to identify variances and help manage tasks on project planning.
* Collaborate with program team members and departments to establish plans and schedules that allocate resources to best achieve program requirements and service internal and external client or customer needs.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering or related field.
* 10 -15 years related experience in Nuclear/ Automotive/ Heavy Engineering/ Metals Industry / Manufacturing / Assembly.
* Experience with project management and new product introduction into manufacturing.
* Analytical capabilities to identify critical schedule paths and improve engineering / supply chain timelines.
* Demonstrated skills in internal operational partner relationship management.
* Advance level PMI certification in Project Management.
* Experience of Engineering Component Manufacturing systems.
* Experience with engineering product development including design phases, manufacturing processes and global supply chain management.
* Familiarization with Kaizen, Lean Operations, FMEA's, DMAIC, DFMAs, POCA cycles.
* Familiarization with Microsoft Project, P6 or other scheduling software.

We are committed to transparency and equity in all of our people practices. The base salary range for this position, which is dependent upon experience, qualifications and skills, is estimated to be $144,000 to $180,000 per year.
 
 
**Why Westinghouse?**
**Benefits**
**Our benefits package is tailored to meet the diverse needs of our employees, while also promoting wellness and career growth. The following are representative of what we offer:**

* Comprehensive Medical benefits which could include medical, dental, vision, prescription coverage and Health Savings Account (HSA) with employer contributions options
* Wellness Programs designed to support employees in maintaining their health and well-being including Employee Assistance Program providing support for our employees and their household members
* 401(k) with Company Match Contributions to support employees' retirement
* Paid Vacations and Company Holidays
* Opportunities for Flexible Work Arrangements to promote work-life balance
* Educational Reimbursement and Comprehensive Career Programs to help employees grow in their careers
* Global Recognition and Service Programs to celebrate employee accomplishments and service
* Employee Referral Program

* Teamwork and Accountability

**While our Global Headquarters are located in Cranberry Township, PA, we have over 11,000 employees working at locations in 19 different countries. You can learn more by visiting**

card.description:
**Bold Thinking. World Changing.**
At SkyWater, our ingenuity helps improve lives around the world by manufacturing U.S. made semiconductors that are essential ingredients of modern life. Automotive safety enhancements, life-saving medical devices, consumer electronics and American security require semiconductors. Working in our Minnesota headquarters, Florida, or Texas location — employees join together to improve the world.
 
 
**Explore what’s possible.**
Joining our U.S. - based team means contributing to and learning about the commercialization of some of the most exciting technologies the world has ever seen. We are turning “science fiction” into everyday reality through technologies such as superconducting, 3D integrated circuits or computer chips, carbon nanotubes, photonic logic devices, micro electro-mechanical systems and other emerging device topologies. We manufacture products for aerospace and defense, medical, automotive, consumer and industrial markets, to name a few. Our customers include emerging leaders who rely on our intellectual property security and quality manufacturing services.
 
 
**Step into the future.**
SkyWater’s values of Integrity, Excellence, Collaboration, Empowerment and Growth Mindset guide us to cultivate an empowered, learning environment. We also invest in developing highly skilled, dedicated employees — and employees who are entering the workforce for the first time, from the military, and a variety of educational backgrounds.
 
 
**Are you bold thinking? Find your place on our team and help us change the world!**
The
**Thin Films and CMP Engineering Senior Manager**
leads Thins/CMP operations in a 200 mm high-volume semiconductor manufacturing facility in Austin, Texas. This role is directly accountable for delivering measurable results in process stability, cost reduction, tool productivity, and continuous yield improvement across mature technology nodes. The ideal candidate will balance strong technical expertise with the operational leadership required to support New Product Development (NPD) and maintain reliable, high-throughput manufacturing.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities Include**

* Lead, develop, and hold accountable a team of ThinFilms/CMP engineers supporting 24/7 fab operations and development.
* Support New Product Development (NPD) by partnering with design and integration teams to develop and stabilize new lithography layers and processes.
* Own and drive results for lithography processes on mature nodes, ensuring high uptime, repeatability, and yield performance against strict production KPIs.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on defect density reduction, overlay control, and CD uniformity.
* Utilize structured problem-solving to contain and address process issues, ensuring timely resolution and sustained results.
* Oversee process control systems, including SPC, FDC, and other control strategies.
* Maintain and improve process documentation, recipes, and control plans.
* Support technology transfers, customer qualifications, and process improvements, taking ownership of project timelines and deliverables.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, or related field (advanced degree a plus).
* 8+ years of semiconductor manufacturing experience, preferably in 150 mm/200 mm fabs.
* 3+ years of leadership or supervisory experience in a production environment with a proven track record of performance management.
* Strong background in Thin Films and CMP for mature technology nodes.
* Expertise with Thin Films and CMP processes, metrology, and control.
* Experience with SPC, DOE, FMEA, and yield improvement methodologies.
* Proven ability to lead teams and drive accountability in a high-volume manufacturing environment.
* Strong focus on operational excellence, tool utilization, and cycle time reduction.
* Ability to prioritize and manage competing production demands while maintaining a results-oriented focus.
* Effective cross-functional communication with manufacturing, integration, and maintenance teams.
* Results-driven mindset with a focus on measurable yield, cost, and throughput.
* 8D and structured problem-solving mentality.

SkyWater offers an exciting environment where the brightest semiconductor minds come together to achieve exceptional results. We offer a competitive salary and an opportunity to participate in incentive plans as well as other employee financial benefits, including a 401 (k) match and life insurance.
 
 
Additionally, SkyWater offers a comprehensive benefits package which promotes a healthy life. This includes benefit eligibility day one, medical, dental, mental health benefits, vision, legal planning, short- and long-term disability, paid time off, paid holidays, an on-site cafeteria, fitness facility, and self-serve market.
 
 
SkyWater complies with federal and state disability laws and makes reasonable accommodations for applicants and employees with disabilities unless doing so would cause an undue hardship. Alternative methods of applying for employment are available to individuals unable to submit an application through this site because of a disability. To request reasonable accommodations, to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please contact Human Resources at 952-851-5200 or Recruiting@SkyWatertechnology.com.

We will never ask applicants to pay fees, purchase equipment or gift cards, or provide financial information before a formal offer of employment has been accepted. With a vision rooted in the wellbeing and inclusive engagement of our team members, our customers, their end users and our communities, people are the heart of what we do and who we are. It is our values that unite us and guide us in everything that we do, including how we operate, behave and interact to foster a workplace where every team member feels valued and empowered to contribute their best.
 
 
Our values include: Growing our People, Building Belonging, Innovating Responsibly, Delivering Excellence and Creating Customer Success.
 
 
As a team member, you will engage in impactful work through global collaboration and the use of emerging technologies, join an inclusive culture where every team member is valued and working toward a greater purpose, and be empowered to reach your full potential through various development programs designed to accelerate your growth.
 
 
Plexus offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support team members' wellbeing, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, paid time off, retirement savings, and opportunities for professional development. We also prioritize work-life balance and offer a variety of perks to enhance the team member experience. For more information, visit our US benefits website at usbenefits.plexus.com. To provide leadership and direction to the Manufacturing Engineering team(s) from a functional perspective. Manage the Manufacturing Engineering function in line with functional specific strategies, process and systems development, people development, employee relations, plant level metrics.

* Lead manufacturing-engineering excellence by collaborating with various functional leads to ensure engineering capability meets or exceeds manufacturing standards for quality product delivery.
* Support Program Management initiatives and activities to meet or exceed customer expectations.
* Lead process/product/equipment engineering activities in compliance with Plexus Core Values to meet industry standards, regulatory and customer requirements.
* Provide technical leadership to site operations, establish a technology roadmap, and collaborate with corporate and regional technical teams to achieve lower costs and higher manufacturing returns.
* Responsible to exemplify and hold their team accountable to demonstrating the Plexus Core Values. Leader will focus on evaluating potential, driving succession planning, and ensuring their employees receive the development and coaching required to realize their full potential.

* Bachelor’s Degree with 8 or more years of related experience is preferred. An equivalent combination of education and/or experience will be considered.
* Proven leadership skills and management experience.

At Plexus, our vision is to help create the products that build a better world. Driven by a passion for excellence, we partner with leading Aerospace/Defense, Healthcare/Life Sciences and Industrial companies to design, manufacture and service some of the world’s most transformative products, including advanced surgical systems, diagnostic instruments, healthcare imaging equipment, mission critical aerospace systems, and electric vehicle (EV) charging solutions. Visit Plexus.com to learn more about our unwavering commitment to our vision.
 
 
**When we invest in our people, we invest in building a better world.**
With a vision rooted in the wellbeing and inclusive engagement of our team members, our customers, their end users and our communities, people are the heart of what we do and who we are. It is our values that unite us and guide us in everything that we do, including how we operate, behave and interact to foster a workplace where every team member feels valued and empowered to contribute their best.
 
 
Our values include: Growing our People, Building Belonging, Innovating Responsibly, Delivering Excellence and Creating Customer Success.
 
 
As a team member, you will engage in impactful work through global collaboration and the use of emerging technologies, join an inclusive culture where every team member is valued and working toward a greater purpose, and be empowered to reach your full potential through various development programs designed to accelerate your growth.
 
 
Plexus offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support team members' wellbeing, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, paid time off, retirement savings, and opportunities for professional development. We also prioritize work-life balance and offer a variety of perks to enhance the team member experience. For more information, visit our US benefits website at usbenefits.plexus.com. Our commitment to pay range transparency fosters an equitable workplace, where everyone can feel valued. The annual compensation range for this position is stated below. The salary offered within this range will be based upon the geographic location, work experience, education, licensure requirements and/or skill level. Salary Range:
 
 
$132,500.00 - $198,700.00
 
 
**Purpose Statement:**
To provide leadership and direction to the Manufacturing Engineering team(s) from a functional perspective. Manage the Manufacturing Engineering function in line with functional specific strategies, process and systems development, people development, employee relations, plant level metrics.
 
 
**Key Job Accountabilities**

* Lead manufacturing-engineering excellence by collaborating with various functional leads to ensure engineering capability meets or exceeds manufacturing standards for quality product delivery.
* Support Program Management initiatives and activities to meet or exceed customer expectations.
* Lead process/product/equipment engineering activities in compliance with Plexus Core Values to meet industry standards, regulatory and customer requirements.
* Provide technical leadership to site operations, establish a technology roadmap, and collaborate with corporate and regional technical teams to achieve lower costs and higher manufacturing returns.
* Responsible to exemplify and hold their team accountable to demonstrating the Plexus Core Values. Leader will focus on evaluating potential, driving succession planning, and ensuring their employees receive the development and coaching required to realize their full potential.

**Education/Experience Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s Degree with 8 or more years of related experience is preferred. An equivalent combination of education and/or experience will be considered.
* Proven leadership skills and management experience.
